A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete metric space]].
Let $\sequence {U_n}$ be a sequence of [[Definition:Open Set (Metric Space)|open]] [[Definition:Everywhere Dense|dense]] subsets of $X$.
Then $\displaystyle \bigcap_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty U_n$ is dense in $X$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a complete metric space and $F_1 \supseteq F_2 \supseteq \cdots$ non-empty [[Definition:Closed Set (Metric Space)|closed sets]] with $\map {\operatorname {diam} } {F_n} \to 0$.
Then $\displaystyle \bigcap_n F_n$ is a single point.

substitutions.the nested closed sets F_n: closed balls chosen inside W and the successive U_n

derived.the intersection point: a point of W lying in every U_n

object_map.reformulation: Reduce density of the intersection to building a nested sequence of closed balls inside the open dense sets.

validity_conditions: Each U_n must be open and dense, so that it meets every open ball in an open set.
Completeness is essential; the rationals are a countable union of points.
proof_plan:
Let $W$ be a non-empty open set.
It suffices to show $W \cap \displaystyle \bigcap_n U_n \ne \O$.

As $U_1$ is open and dense, $W \cap U_1$ is non-empty and open.
Choose a closed ball $\overline {B_1} \subseteq W \cap U_1$ of radius less than $1$.
Inductively, as $U_{n + 1}$ is open and dense, choose a closed ball $\overline {B_{n + 1} } \subseteq B_n \cap U_{n + 1}$ of radius less than $\dfrac 1 {n + 1}$.

By [[Cantor's Intersection Theorem]], $\displaystyle \bigcap_n \overline {B_n} = \set x$.
Then $x \in W$ and $x \in U_n$ for every $n$.
This is the [[Baire Category Theorem]].
{{qed}}
